scenes.vo: Ninety-two students played the ROE practice maze on the twenty-third of November. Every step they took was logged. This is that log, replayed.
Here, everyone starts at the same moment, so all ninety-two runs play side by side. Each dot is one student, coloured by their final score.

items.text: One student. Darker blue means a higher final score
A green ring is a task solved, red is a wrong answer

scenes.vo: In the first five minutes, most head straight for the three-mark tasks near the start: the router terminal and the help desks.
Follow one of the top scorers. icy-seal-42 solves all twelve tasks, including both locked rooms, in twenty-seven minutes, with one wrong answer.

items.text: tasks solved, every one that could be marked
minutes from start to the last task

scenes.vo: Traps slow everyone down. One meeting trap in Open Office A4 caught players seventy-two times. Some players left notes on the floor to warn the next person.

callout.title: A note left two tiles away

items.quote: do NOT go 2 steps from here in north direction. there's trap

scenes.vo: By the end, the class splits in two. Twenty-one students scored nothing: five never moved, and nine left within ten minutes. Most of the rest landed between eighteen and twenty-five.
The top of the board comes down to one door. The vault opens only when three students stand on three red pads, and push together.
Forty-six students pressed those pads. In nineteen hours, the door opened four times. Only ten students ever solved the task inside.
Open Office B7, right outside the door, is where students spent the most time. The chat there is mostly one message, again and again.

items.quote: push the door we need 1 more person

scenes.vo: Part of the reason may be timing. The world stayed open for nineteen hours, and no more than sixteen students were ever online at the same moment.
Every student who got through the door scored twenty-four or more. All five top scores of twenty-seven came through it.
All of this comes from one script. Point it at any synced maze log and it builds this page: the replay, the heatmap and these findings, with handles in place of emails.
